pr_title: Ensure states table rebuild still happens if the event_id index was removed
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
If `ix_states_event_id` index was removed but the foreign key still exists, the states table would not get rebuilt. This should not happen under normal circumstances but can if:

- The index was removed manually
- Home Assistant was restarted forcefully in the middle of a previous migration from years ago
- The system ran out of disk space during a previous migration

issue_context.title: Purge get stuck deleting events and causes recorder to stop writing to the DB until HA is restarted after previous rebuild failed due to out of disk space
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Symptoms are basically identical to issue #117263, but @bdraco told to make a new bug:

- recorder.purge stops new data from being recorded--my graphs flatline.
- happens daily at 4:12 am and via manual service calls
- single cpu core goes to 100%

But there are a couple of differences:

- disk reads of ~50+ mb/s were occurring, but I tried increasing the VM's ram allocation from 8 gb to 20 gb, and this stopped the constant reads.
- issue started for me when upgrading to 2024.7.1 (I skipped .0)


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2024.6.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

recorder

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/recorder/

### Diagnostics information

The logger section of my configuration.yaml has:

```
logger:
  default: error
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.rainmachine: critical
    sqlalchemy: debug
```

HA was restarted after the changes above.  The recorder.purge service call was triggered manually and symptoms above were observed.  After a little over an hour of those symptoms, here's the content of the logs:

 
[home-assistant_2024-07-13T18-47-58.907Z.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16203338/home-assistant_2024-07-13T18-47-58.907Z.zip)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
sqlalchemy debug output.
```


### Additional information

My previous comments starting here might be of use: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/117263#issuecomment-2223048031
